Traditional Pork Tamales for Día de los Muertos

Served at: Dia de los Muertos

Serves 8-10 (makes about 30-40 tamales)Prep 3 hoursCook 2 hours

Tamales are a cornerstone of Día de los Muertos celebrations, lovingly prepared to honor departed loved ones. These savory bundles of masa, often filled with rich pork in a chile sauce, are placed on altars as offerings and shared among family, symbolizing sustenance and connection across generations.

Ingredients

  • 1 (10 oz / 280 g) package dried corn husks
  • 3 pounds (1.4 kg) pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
  • 1 large white onion, quartered
  • 4 cloves garlic, smashed
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 6-8 dried guajillo chiles, stems and seeds removed
  • 3-4 dried ancho chiles, stems and seeds removed
  • 2 cups (480 ml) chicken broth (plus more for cooking pork)
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1/4 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 4 cups (480 g) masa harina para tamales (specifically for tamales, not instant corn masa flour)
  • 1 1/2 cups (340 g) lard (manteca), at room temperature, or vegetable shortening
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 3 1/2 - 4 cups (840-960 ml) warm chicken broth

Method

  1. Place corn husks in a large bowl or pot, cover with hot water, and weigh down with a plate to keep them submerged. Let soak for at least 1 hour, or until pliable.
  2. In a large pot, combine pork shoulder, half of the quartered onion, 2 smashed garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Cover with water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 1.5-2 hours, or until pork is very tender and easily shredded. Remove pork from broth, reserving 2 cups (480 ml) of the cooking liquid. Shred the pork using two forks.
  3. While pork cooks, prepare the chiles. Toast guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side until fragrant. Be careful not to burn them. Place toasted chiles in a bowl, cover with hot water, and let soak for 20-30 minutes until softened. Drain the chiles, reserving a little soaking liquid.
  4. In a blender, combine the softened chiles, the remaining half of the quartered onion, 2 smashed garlic cloves, 2 cups (480 ml) reserved pork cooking liquid, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Blend until very smooth. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
  5. In a large skillet or pot, combine the shredded pork with the strained chile sauce. Simmer over low heat for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Set aside to cool slightly.
  6. In a very large bowl, beat the room temperature lard (or shortening) with an electric mixer on high speed for 5 minutes, until light and fluffy.
  7. In a separate bowl, whisk together the masa harina, baking powder, and salt. Gradually add the masa harina mixture to the beaten lard, alternating with the warm chicken broth, mixing until a soft, spreadable dough forms. The dough should be light and fluffy. To test if the masa is ready, drop a small piece (about 1/2 teaspoon) into a cup of cold water; if it floats, it's ready. If not, beat for another minute or two and retest.
  8. Drain the softened corn husks and pat them dry. Take one corn husk, shiny side up, with the wider end at the top. Spread about 2-3 tablespoons of masa evenly over the wider half of the husk, leaving a 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) border on the sides and top.
  9. Place 1-2 tablespoons of the pork filling down the center of the masa.
  10. Fold one side of the husk over the filling, then fold the other side over, overlapping. Fold the narrow bottom end of the husk up towards the filling. Leave the top open. Repeat with remaining masa, filling, and husks.
  11. Arrange tamales upright in a steamer basket, open-end up, being careful not to pack them too tightly. If you have a lot, you can layer them. Pour 1-2 inches (2.5-5 cm) of water into the bottom of the steamer pot, ensuring the water does not touch the tamales. Bring water to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover tightly, and steam for 1.5-2 hours.
  12. Tamales are done when the masa easily pulls away from the corn husk. If not, continue steaming for another 15-30 minutes and recheck.
  13. Let tamales rest for 10-15 minutes off the heat before serving. Serve warm.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian option, fill tamales with cheese and jalapeños or a mixture of roasted vegetables.
  • Tamales can be made ahead of time and frozen. To reheat, steam from frozen for about 30-45 minutes.
  • Ensure your masa is light and fluffy; this is key to tender tamales. If it's too dry, add a little more broth, one tablespoon at a time.
